claims.text: Environmental TEM with in-situ heating can investigate the thermal behavior of AuCoCuNiPt nanoparticles at the atomic scale.
The investigated AuCoCuNiPt nanoparticles are high-entropy-alloy nanoparticles.
In-situ heating will reveal lattice strain as a structural mediator.
Heating induces atomic diffusion in the nanoparticles.
At 800°C, the lattice parameter will be 10–20% greater than its value at 20°C.
The initial material is identified as AuCoCoCuNiPt nanoparticles.
The initial nanoparticles have a face-centered-cubic structure.
The proposed experiment heats the nanoparticles from 20°C to 800°C.
The proposed heating rates are 1°C/min, 5°C/min, and 10°C/min.
The proposed experiment uses a vacuum environment.
The proposed experiment uses atmospheric pressure.
Lattice strain is defined as deviation of the lattice parameter from its equilibrium value.
Lattice strain is expected to increase with temperature because of thermally induced atomic diffusion.
An increase in thermal energy drives thermally induced atomic diffusion.
Atomic bonding strength decreases as temperature increases, contributing to atomic diffusion.
The lattice-parameter change may depend on heating rate, environment, nanoparticle size, and nanoparticle shape.

contradictions.description: The target composition is written as AuCoCuNiPt in the hypothesis but as AuCoCoCuNiPt in the initial-state field, introducing an extra Co entry.
Vacuum and atmospheric pressure are both specified without indicating that they are separate experimental runs; they cannot simultaneously describe one environmental condition.
